dedupe_keys.name: maxxwave coveragemapper free browser tool for predicted fm and dab coverage maps

description: CoverageMapper is a browser-based tool from the UK company Maxxwave that predicts FM and DAB radio coverage. Launched in September 2026 as community groups prepared expressions of interest for Ofcom's new round of FM community radio licences, it lets a user pick a transmitter location on a map, enter antenna height and power, and download a coverage prediction, usually produced within a minute, with no software installation. Predictions account for terrain, buildings and woodland and use the same planning approach as Ofcom. Saved sites can be re-plotted with other heights and powers to compare locations. The free version supports one transmitter site and powers up to 500 W; Maxxwave's full system adds single frequency network planning, timing and interference analysis, and the company says it will assess feedback before releasing advanced tools. Producer: Maxxwave. Coverage: built for UK licensing, prediction model as described by the company. Access: the tool page loads through scripts and could not be read from the cloud session, so this record rests on the RadioToday launch report of September 2026; no open-source release is known. Licence and cost: free tier limited to one site and 500 W; other terms not read. Caveats: it cannot say whether a frequency is available, and predictions are not a substitute for regulator planning. Simulation uses: coverage predictions feed siting and capacity planning for broadcast networks. Related records: RadioPlanner (platform-radioplanner) and the radio coverage tool (platform-radio-coverage-tool).
